original_question: What concrete limitations do information-theoretic and thermodynamic bounds for feedback-controlled systems impose on the operation and achievable performance of nanotechnology devices and biological systems in which one subsystem uses bidirectional interaction with another subsystem to improve that subsystem's performance?
target_in_paper: Open problem in Section III.C: Limitations to the Operation of Nanotechnology Devices and Biological Systems
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies that the paper poses an open question about how the general information-theoretic and thermodynamic bounds for feedback-controlled systems translate into performance limits for nanotechnology and biological systems, and it recognizes the bidirectional interaction mapping one subsystem as a controller acting on another.
missing_details: Specify which specific bounds (e.g., the Shannon‐information limit ΔH_closed ≤ ΔH_open + I(X;C) and the entropy reduction formula ΔS_info = −k_B∑_{k=1}^M I(X_k;C_k|C_{k−1},…,C_1)) are to be used.
Define explicitly the controlled subsystem (whose performance is enhanced) and the controller subsystem, following the feedback‐controlled framework in the paper.
List the quantitative performance metrics of interest (transport flux, power output, work extraction, entropy reduction, etc.) that will be constrained.
Clarify the role of bidirectional interaction in terms of mutual information exchanged per control step and the distinction between per-step and per-unit-time (nonredundant) information.
State whether the constraints should be expressed for single actuation, repeated correlated actuations, or in the continuous‐time limit, as discussed in Sections II D and II C.
refined_question: For a nanotechnology device or biological system comprising two interacting subsystems—one serving as the feedback controller (C_k) and the other as the controlled system (X_k)—determine how the general information-theoretic limit on closed-loop control (ΔH_closed ≤ ΔH_open + I(X;C) from Section II.B, Eq. (4)) and the thermodynamic entropy-reduction result for repeated correlated feedback actuation (ΔS_info = −k_B∑_{k=1}^M I(X_k;C_k|C_{k−1},…,C_1) from Section II.D, Eq. (14)) impose quantitative constraints on the maximum achievable performance measures—such as transport flux, power output, and work extraction—in such systems, both per control step and per unit time.
justification: The refined question is a direct instantiation of the open problem posed in Section III.C, which asks for the implications of feedback control bounds for nanotechnology and biological systems ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1205.4434)). It explicitly references the information-theoretic bound of Section II.B, Eq. (4) ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1205.4434)) and the entropy-reduction formula of Section II.D, Eq. (14) ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1205.4434)), and includes performance metrics (flux and power) tied to the bounds in Section II.C, Eqs. (5) and (6) ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1205.4434)).
